images.prompt: An International-style graphic: flat geometric shapes on a white field, black and grays with one Swiss-red accent, strict alignment and generous whitespace. Reductive and rational — a diagrammatic image, no shadows, no gradients, no ornament. Subject: a camel's silhouette built entirely from straight integration-route lines and right-angle joins, like a schematic circuit board — a handful of small labeled endpoint nodes (an envelope, a database cylinder, a gear) sit at line terminations along the camel's back and legs, picking out the single Swiss-red accent against otherwise black-on-white line work. The camel reads as a diagram of a routing system, not an illustration of an animal: thin uniform strokes, no shading, no texture, strictly orthographic and flat. Generous whitespace, no text baked in. Target size ~1600x900px, 16:9 landscape; compose for a book cover with the subject centred and safe margins — it is letterboxed into a 16:9 box, so keep nothing important near the edges.
images.alt: A camel's silhouette rendered as a schematic of connected integration routes
images.caption: The book's cover: a camel drawn as a diagram of the routes it carries.

notes: Requested as a syllabus-length course book: 'Apache Camel: An Introduction to Enterprise Integration', organized in seven parts. The issue's Seed concepts field was a markdown outline rather than one concept per line, so it was parsed conservatively: each of the 31 explicitly numbered chapter headings became one concept, its Part heading was kept as `unit`, and its sub-bullets were folded into that concept's `brief`. No concepts were invented, dropped, or reordered. Keep the seven-part progression visible in the table of contents — Foundations, First Routes, Messages, Core Patterns, Real Systems, Reliability and Operations, then the Capstone — since the parts are the spine of the course. Notes and Reference material were both left blank on the request.
